solution: The expression is defined and continuous at \(z = -3\) (the radicand \(z + 6 = 3 > 0\) and \(z \ne 0\)), so the limit is obtained by direct substitution. \(\dfrac{\sqrt{-3 + 6}}{-3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{-3} = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\). Hence the limit is \(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

Since \(243 = 3^5\) and \(27 = 3^3\), with \((-3)^5 = -243\) and \((-3)^3 = -27\), the quotient is \(\dfrac{y^5 - (-3)^5}{y^3 - (-3)^3}\), which is of the form \(\dfrac{0}{0}\). Divide numerator and denominator by \(y - (-3)\) and use \(\lim_{y \to a} \dfrac{y^n - a^n}{y - a} = n a^{n-1}\) with \(a = -3\). The limit \(= \dfrac{5(-3)^4}{3(-3)^2} = \dfrac{5 \times 81}{3 \times 9} = \dfrac{405}{27} = 15\). Hence the limit is \(15\).

Combine the two fractions in the numerator: \(\dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{5 + z}{5z}\). So the expression becomes \(\dfrac{z + 5}{5z(z + 5)} = \dfrac{1}{5z}\) for \(z \ne -5\). Taking \(z \to -5\) gives \(\dfrac{1}{5(-5)} = -\dfrac{1}{25}\). Hence the limit is \(-\dfrac{1}{25}\).
The expression is continuous at \(x = 3\), so substitute directly. \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2(3) + 6}}{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{12}}{3} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\). Hence the limit is \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\).

This is of the form \(\dfrac{0}{0}\) and matches the standard limit \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^n - a^n}{x - a} = n a^{n-1}\) with \(n = -3\) and \(a = 2\). So the limit \(= (-3)(2)^{-4} = -\dfrac{3}{2^4} = -\dfrac{3}{16}\). Hence the limit is \(-\dfrac{3}{16}\).

Since \(125 = 5^3\) and \(3125 = 5^5\), the quotient is \(\dfrac{x^3 - 5^3}{x^5 - 5^5}\), of the form \(\dfrac{0}{0}\). Divide both numerator and denominator by \(x - 5\) and apply \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^n - a^n}{x - a} = n a^{n-1}\) with \(a = 5\). The limit \(= \dfrac{3(5)^2}{5(5)^4} = \dfrac{75}{3125} = \dfrac{3}{125}\). Hence the limit is \(\dfrac{3}{125}\).

Using \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^n - a^n}{x - a} = n a^{n-1}\): the left side is \(\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{x^4 - 1^4}{x - 1} = 4(1)^3 = 4\), and the right side is \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^3 - a^3}{x - a} = 3a^2\). Equating, \(3a^2 = 4\), so \(a^2 = \dfrac{4}{3}\) and \(a = \pm \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\). Hence \(a = \pm \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\).

Write \(n = 1 + 1 + \ldots + 1\) (\(n\) terms) and pair each power with a \(1\), so the expression becomes \(\dfrac{(x - 1) + (x^2 - 1) + \ldots + (x^n - 1)}{x - 1} = \sum_{r=1}^{n} \dfrac{x^r - 1^r}{x - 1}\). Taking \(x \to 1\) and using \(\lim_{x \to 1} \dfrac{x^r - 1^r}{x - 1} = r(1)^{r-1} = r\), the limit \(= 1 + 2 + \ldots + n = \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\). Hence the limit is \(\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\).

The numerator is a difference of squares: \(\left( x^{1/3} - 7^{1/3} \right)\left( x^{1/3} + 7^{1/3} \right) = x^{2/3} - 7^{2/3}\). So the limit is \(\lim_{x \to 7} \dfrac{x^{2/3} - 7^{2/3}}{x - 7} = \dfrac{2}{3}(7)^{2/3 - 1} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 7^{-1/3}\). Hence the limit is \(\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{7}}\).

By \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^k - a^k}{x - a} = k a^{k-1}\) with \(a = 5\), the given condition is \(k \cdot 5^{k-1} = 500\). Trying \(k = 4\): \(4 \times 5^3 = 4 \times 125 = 500\), which satisfies it. Since \(k \cdot 5^{k-1}\) is strictly increasing for \(k > 0\) and is negative for \(k < 0\), no other value works. Hence \(k = 4\).

Put \(t = 1 - x\); as \(x \to 0\), \(t \to 1\). The limit becomes \(\lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{t^8 - 1}{t^2 - 1}\), which is of the form \(\dfrac{0}{0}\). Dividing numerator and denominator by \(t - 1\) and using \(\lim_{t \to 1} \dfrac{t^n - 1^n}{t - 1} = n\), it equals \(\dfrac{8}{2} = 4\). Hence the limit is \(4\).

Subtract and add \(1\) in the numerator and split: \(\dfrac{(1 + x)^{1/3} - 1}{x} - \dfrac{(1 + x)^{1/2} - 1}{x}\). Using the standard limit \(\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(1 + x)^n - 1}{x} = n\), this tends to \(\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{2 - 3}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{6}\). Hence the limit is \(-\dfrac{1}{6}\).

At \(y = 1\) both parts vanish, since \(\sqrt[3]{7 + 1} = 2\). Put \(u = 7 + y\), so \(u \to 8\) and \(y - 1 = u - 8\). The limit becomes \(2 \lim_{u \to 8} \dfrac{u - 8}{u^{1/3} - 8^{1/3}} = \dfrac{2}{\lim_{u \to 8} \frac{u^{1/3} - 8^{1/3}}{u - 8}} = \dfrac{2}{\frac{1}{3}(8)^{-2/3}} = \dfrac{2}{\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}} = 2 \times 12 = 24\). Hence the limit is \(24\).

Put \(u = z + 2\) and \(b = a + 2\); as \(z \to a\), \(u \to b\) and \(z - a = u - b\). The limit becomes \(\lim_{u \to b} \dfrac{u^{3/2} - b^{3/2}}{u - b} = \dfrac{3}{2} b^{1/2}\). Substituting back \(b = a + 2\), the limit is \(\dfrac{3\sqrt{a + 2}}{2}\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(x - 7\): the limit is \(\dfrac{\lim_{x \to 7} \frac{x^3 - 7^3}{x - 7}}{\lim_{x \to 7} \frac{x^{1/2} - 7^{1/2}}{x - 7}}\). The numerator limit is \(3(7)^2 = 147\) and the denominator limit is \(\dfrac{1}{2}(7)^{-1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{7}}\). So the limit \(= 147 \times 2\sqrt{7} = 294\sqrt{7}\). Hence the limit is \(294\sqrt{7}\).

There are \(n\) powers, so write \(n\) as \(n\) ones and pair them off: the expression equals \(\sum_{r=1}^{n} \dfrac{x^{2r-1} - 1}{x - 1}\). As \(x \to 1\), each term tends to \(2r - 1\), so the limit \(= 1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots + (2n - 1) = n^2\). Hence the limit is \(n^2\).

Here \(f(x) = 2x + 3\), \(a = 2\), \(l = 7\). Then \(|f(x) - l| = |2x + 3 - 7| = |2x - 4| = 2|x - 2|\). So \(|f(x) - 7| < \varepsilon\) holds exactly when \(2|x - 2| < \varepsilon\), that is when \(|x - 2| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{2}\). Hence choosing \(\delta = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{2}\) works: whenever \(|x - 2| < \delta\) we get \(|2x + 3 - 7| < \varepsilon\).

Here \(f(x) = 3x + 2\), \(a = -3\), \(l = -7\). Then \(|f(x) - l| = |3x + 2 + 7| = |3x + 9| = 3|x + 3|\). So \(|f(x) + 7| < \varepsilon\) holds exactly when \(3|x + 3| < \varepsilon\), that is when \(|x + 3| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{3}\). Hence choosing \(\delta = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{3}\) works: whenever \(|x + 3| < \delta\) we get \(|3x + 2 - (-7)| < \varepsilon\).

Here \(f(x) = x^2 - 1\), \(a = 2\), \(l = 3\), and \(|f(x) - l| = |x^2 - 4| = |x - 2| \cdot |x + 2|\). First restrict \(|x - 2| < 1\), which gives \(1 < x < 3\) and hence \(|x + 2| < 5\). Then \(|x^2 - 4| < 5|x - 2|\), which is less than \(\varepsilon\) whenever \(|x - 2| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{5}\). Hence \(\delta = \min\left\{ 1, \dfrac{\varepsilon}{5} \right\}\) works.

Here \(f(x) = x^2 + x + 1\), \(a = 1\), \(l = 3\), and \(|f(x) - l| = |x^2 + x - 2| = |x - 1| \cdot |x + 2|\). First restrict \(|x - 1| < 1\), which gives \(0 < x < 2\) and hence \(|x + 2| < 4\). Then \(|x^2 + x - 2| < 4|x - 1|\), which is less than \(\varepsilon\) whenever \(|x - 1| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{4}\). Hence \(\delta = \min\left\{ 1, \dfrac{\varepsilon}{4} \right\}\) works.
